About me

From architecture to code: building with structure and empathy.

I trained as an architect, with a master’s degree from the Polytechnic of Bari, and I learned to turn a brief, a site and a long list of constraints into spaces people enjoy using. Between 2020 and 2022 I moved into web development through two bootcamps, because I realised that screens are the new spaces: people move through them, get lost in them, or feel at home.

Since then I have worked on banking, insurance, retail and healthcare products as a frontend engineer who owns the UX/UI, and I added Java and Spring Boot to deliver full-stack products end to end. Today I work between designers, developers and business teams, and I’m growing towards product design. I also earned a bachelor’s degree in IT for Digital Enterprises at Pegaso Digital University.

How architecture makes me a better developer

Systems thinkingA building is a system of structure, flows and use. I apply the same logic to design systems and component libraries, like ARTEA: 27 components reused in three applications.
Designing movementArchitects design how people move through a space. I design how users move through a product: clear navigation, sensible flows and fewer errors (−40% errors on an insurance platform).
Precision within constraintsEvery project has budgets, regulations and physics. I’m used to finding elegant solutions inside technical, legal and business limits, and to documenting them (UML, specifications).
Collaboration across disciplinesArchitects coordinate engineers, clients and builders. I bring the same habit to stakeholders, designers and developers: gather requirements, prototype in Figma, validate early.
